entry.title: Graph Theory and Optical Response in Nanoparticle Assemblies

link.title: Graph Theory and Optical Response in Nanoparticle Assemblies

entry.content: I’m excited to share a recent MRS Bulletin Materials News article I coauthored with Ilya Mazalov, “Graph theory reveals how disorder enhances optical response in nanoparticle assemblies.” In the piece, we highlight how graph-based analysis can help reveal the relationship between structural disorder and optical behavior in nanoparticle assemblies, offering a different way to understand and potentially design complex nanomaterials.
entry.summary: Sharing our MRS Bulletin Materials News article on how disorder shapes optical behavior in nanoparticle assemblies.

entry.title: Shape-Shifting Nanoparticles for CO₂ Conversion
entry.content: I’m excited to share a recent MRS Bulletin Materials News article I coauthored with Ilya Mazalov, “Shape-shifting nanoparticles introduce dynamic path for CO₂ conversion.” The piece highlights how dynamically restructuring nanoparticles can open new pathways for catalytic CO₂ conversion, showing how changes in particle structure can directly influence reaction behavior.
entry.summary: Sharing our MRS Bulletin Materials News article on dynamically restructuring nanoparticles for catalytic CO₂ conversion.

entry.title: Starting at Micron AMAIS
entry.content:
This summer, I started as an intern at Micron Technology on the Advanced Modeling and AI Solutions (AMAIS) team in Boise, ID.

I’m excited to bring my background in AI for scientific computing into an industry setting, working on problems where modeling, data, and engineering meet at semiconductor scale.

My project focuses on building a material agent that interfaces multiple simulation and data analysis tools at Micron, providing a more robust and automated workflow.

I’m grateful for the opportunity to learn from and work alongside the engineers at Micron, and I’m excited for what this summer will bring.
entry.summary: Beginning my internship with Micron's Advanced Modeling and AI Solutions team.

entry.title: Meeting Scene Reporter
entry.content:
I was excited to serve as a Meeting Scene Reporter at the Materials Research Society (MRS) Spring 2026 Meeting, highlighting symposium talks and making emerging materials research more accessible to a broader audience.

Pieces I covered:

  1. AI-Driven Integration of Molecular Modeling and Experimental Data. MRS Meeting Scene, Symposium MT04, 2026.

  2. Accelerating Battery Materials Discovery with AI- and Physics-Powered Molecular Universe Platform. MRS Meeting Scene, Symposium MT02, 2026.

  3. Solvation Structure Modulation in Aqueous Electrolytes: Stabilizing Pyrazine Radicals and Facilitating Electrochemical Nitrate Reduction. MRS Meeting Scene, Symposium MT04, 2026.

  4. Bespoke Machine-Learned Interatomic Potentials — Pushing the Limits of Accuracy and Efficiency. MRS Meeting Scene, Symposium MT03, 2026.

  5. Optimization Method of Monomer Composites’ Ratio Leading to the Best Polymer Property by Using Machine Learning Method and Quasi-Quantum Computing Method. MRS Meeting Scene, Symposium MT04, 2026.

It was a great opportunity to engage with emerging research across materials science and communicate it to a broader audience.
entry.summary: Covering AI and materials research for MRS Meeting Scene at the Spring 2026 conference.
